report.summary: CoreDNS experienced an internal CPU saturation and latency spike starting at 13:23 UTC on 2026-10-14, which led to UDP query timeouts for external domains. This directly caused downstream getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN resolution errors in notification-service beginning at 13:25 UTC, resulting in intermittent notification failures.

supporting.note: Shows coredns error rates started rising at 13:23:00 UTC, directly preceding the notification-service error spike.
Shows coredns p99 latency spiked from ~3ms to over 2112ms starting at 13:23:00 UTC.
Shows coredns CPU utilization spiked past 100% starting at 13:23:00 UTC.
Shows coredns logging UDP timeout errors resolving sms-vendor.example.net starting at 13:24:03 UTC.
Shows the exact onset of the error rate anomaly at 13:25:00 UTC, immediately following coredns degradation.
Shows persistent getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN for push-provider starting at 13:25:05 UTC.
Shows persistent getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN for sms-vendor starting at 13:25:10 UTC.
Past incident confirms prior occurrences of EAI_AGAIN errors across cluster services due to CoreDNS issues.

contradicting.note: CoreDNS overall RPS showed no major spike or anomaly, staying relatively stable around 3500 req/s.

supporting.note: Shows CoreDNS timing out specifically when querying UDP for sms-vendor.example.net.
Shows notification-service failing to resolve sms-vendor.example.net with EAI_AGAIN.

contradicting.note: CoreDNS CPU utilization spiked to 105.92%, indicating internal resource contention rather than simple pass-through network packet loss.
CoreDNS errors started internally at 13:23 UTC before vendor-specific queries failed.

facts.text: CoreDNS latency_p99_ms experienced an anomaly starting at 2026-10-14T13:23:00+00:00, peaking at 2112.52 ms.
CoreDNS error_rate_pct experienced an anomaly starting at 2026-10-14T13:23:00+00:00, peaking at 22.72%.
CoreDNS cpu_pct experienced an anomaly starting at 2026-10-14T13:23:00+00:00, peaking at 105.92%.
CoreDNS logged UDP timeout errors trying to resolve sms-vendor.example.net starting at 2026-10-14T13:24:03+00:00.
Notification-service error_rate_pct shows an anomaly onset at 2026-10-14T13:25:00+00:00, with error rates jumping from a baseline of ~0.27% to a peak of 26.58%.
Notification-service logged getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN errors for fcm.push-provider.example.com starting at 2026-10-14T13:25:05+00:00.
Notification-service logged getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN errors for sms-vendor.example.net starting at 2026-10-14T13:25:10+00:00.

assumptions: The CPU spike and query timeouts in CoreDNS were triggered by upstream recursive resolver latency or a burst of specific query patterns that exhausted CoreDNS worker threads.

timeline.event: CoreDNS metrics (error rate, latency p99, and CPU) begin abnormal upward trend.
CoreDNS logs UDP timeout errors resolving sms-vendor.example.net.
Notification-service logs getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN for push-provider.
Notification-service logs getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN for sms-vendor.

recommended_actions.action: Scale up or restart CoreDNS pods to mitigate CPU saturation and resolve active DNS timeout loops.
recommended_actions.rationale: CoreDNS CPU utilization exceeded 105% and p99 latency spiked past 2100ms, causing cascading name resolution failures across the cluster.

recommended_actions.action: Implement local caching or negative caching tuning for DNS resolution in notification-service to reduce cluster-wide DNS lookup load.
recommended_actions.rationale: Past incidents and current logs indicate that DNS resolution dependency issues severely impact outbound service calls.

recommended_actions.action: Review CoreDNS resource limits, horizontal autoscaling configurations, and ndots settings cluster-wide.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevent future CPU exhaustion and excessive amplification lookups as seen in past similar incidents.
